deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It holds Riemann's reading notes from the Hartenstein edition of J. F. Herbart's Sämmtliche Werke. The previous and next pages show that it belongs to the same set of excerpts on psychology and metaphysics in the 'Naturphilosophie' bundle. The archive label at the top right reads 'Riemann 13', and the circled folio number is 67.

(1) Herbart, Werke Bd. VI, Psychologie als Wissenschaft, Analytischer Theil, Erster Abschnitt 'Vom geistigen Leben überhaupt'.
- From p. 204, a summary passage. The preceding chapters showed what is general in the psychological mechanism of representations arising from sensations. Hence space, time, number and the categories are the same for all minds, even if their senses were not the same; the difference lies only in more or less development.
- Riemann then lists the chapters: Cap. 3 'Von räumlichen und zeitlichen Vorstellungen' (pp. 114–150); Cap. 4 'Von den ersten Spuren des sogenannten oberen Erkenntnißvermögens' (pp. 150–188); Cap. 5 'Von der Apperception, dem inneren Sinne, und der Aufmerksamkeit' (pp. 188–205).

(2) Under the underlined heading 'Causalität', a long excerpt from p. 154. All our representations, because they are together in one soul, would present one single, undifferentiated object, spatial as well as temporal, if it were not for the mutual inhibitions (Hemmungen) and oppositions of representations. Whatever the inhibitions do not separate, directly or indirectly, stays together and is represented as one.
- Example of the bell: colour, shape, sound, hardness and coldness are fused into one thing. The real question is why the bell is not also fused with the beam it hangs from, or the tree with the soil.
- Answer: that total fusion is the original mode of apprehension. Changing surroundings, things moving from their places, the shifting range of what is taken in at once, and changes of the observer's standpoint all produce new complexions of representations. These enter inhibition relations with the earlier ones, and this yields 'Grenze und Theil' (boundary and part): the tree in the forest, the forest in the landscape.
- The same mechanism of association underlies expectation of similar cases. It links, for the soothsayer, sign with foretold outcome, and, for the physicist, effect with cause. Originally every event is a 'Vorzeichen' (omen) only because its representation and that of its successor meet and fuse in one consciousness.
- Further experience breaks the bond in many places: sequences with opposite outcomes after the same beginning inhibit each other. Often-repeated similar sequences reinforce each other and become the basis of everyday practical wisdom (Lebensklugheit).

(3) Herbart, Werke Bd. V, p. 501, §102 'Unterschied des Geistigen und Leiblichen'.
- Many complexions of perceived marks ('Dinge') appear mostly as endpoints of series that start from other things, or as starting points only insofar as they were earlier endpoints. These are called matter (Stoff, Materie).
- The rarer things from which series start as often as they arrive are thought of as spirits: sources and origins of events.
- The spring (Quelle) is the natural symbol of the spiritual. Yet, on reflection, the spring itself is merely passive; we project into it our own state, in which a representation strives to drive forth the series that issues from it. The next page continues this passage.

The purpose of these notes appears to be Riemann's study of Herbart's psychological mechanism: how unity of objects, part–whole structure, spatial/temporal form and the causal concept arise from interacting representations. This is background for his own Naturphilosophie and epistemology fragments. No computation, formula or derivation appears anywhere on the page.

transcription_corrections: Top right: archive label 'Riemann 13'; circled folio number '67' at right margin.

p. 204 line: 'der physiologische Mechanismus' is more likely 'der psychologische Mechanismus' (Herbart's term). 'Die vorhergehenden Capitel waren' is probably 'wiesen hin' / 'weisen hin auf das Allgemeine'.
'Dieser Raum, Zeit, Zahlen, Kategorien' is more plausibly 'Daher Raum, Zeit, Zahlen, Kategorien, die nämlichen für Alle'.
Struck-out marginal reference before 'Cap. 3' appears as '[-p. 114-]' (deleted), consistent with the transcription.
'oder auf der Uhr bald mehr bald weniger von ihnen zusammenfaßte' is very likely 'oder auch der Blick bald mehr bald weniger von ihnen zusammenfaßte'.
'Die fortgehende Erfahrung [deleted word] aber zerreißt' is consistent; the deleted word is illegible.
§102: 'Wer sich ein Thier denken will' is probably 'Wer sich ein Thun denken will' (an activity, fitting the context of source/series).
'Stoff, als Materie, die sich nicht von selbst bewegt' – the manuscript appears to read 'die aus sich nichts ... bewegt'; uncertain.
Heading 'Causalität' is underlined/boxed in the manuscript, and 'Glocke', 'Grenze und Theil', 'ähnlicher Fälle', 'Stoff', 'Geister', 'Quelle', 'Endpunkte', 'Anfangspunkte' are underlined by Riemann.
